**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/23 (Tue) 14:16
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Roland RP-107 is an entry-level digital piano with 88 weighted keys.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 competes in a crowded sub-$1500 market alongside Kawai KDP 75, KDP 120, and Yamaha Arias YDP 145 and 165.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 replaces the RP-102 model.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 features the new BMC chip and updated Supernatural piano engine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 provides a similar piano tone experience to the Roland FP-30X and GP3 digital grand piano.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 does not have discrete audio jacks; line-out is through the headphone jack.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Supernatural engine of the RP-107 provides a fat attack and works well for contemporary and jazz playing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 features PHA-4 key action, which is professional-grade, with a triple sensor and escapement (let-off).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The key weighting of the RP-107 is slightly on the heavier side, similar to a large upright or small baby grand piano.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 has 8-watt speakers that provide more detail than other models in the price range due to an efficient design and front tone ports.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 comes with a stand, triple pedal, and bench included.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 has 15 tones available, including e-pianos and strings, with the ability to layer sounds.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 is only available in a black finish.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 features Bluetooth MIDI and audio connectivity and is compatible with the Roland Piano App.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The RP-107 comes with over 300 preloaded songs, including play-along repertoire from popular method books.
